title: The pricing toolkit
story: The shop's new website needs a few small functions that other code will call: one to price a pizza, one to keep numbers in a range, and one to format prices. They're tested by calling them directly with different values, so they must **return** their answers, not print them.

requirements.text: `pizza_price(size, toppings=0)` returns the price: size `"s"` costs 7, `"m"` costs 9, `"l"` costs 11, plus 1.25 for each topping.
`pizza_price` uses 0 toppings when that argument is left out.
`clamp(value, low, high)` returns value, but never less than low or more than high.
`money(amount)` returns a string: `£` followed by the amount with exactly two decimal places.
None of the three functions print anything. They only return values.
Your file doesn't do anything else when it runs: no input, no prints at the top level.

steps: Define the three functions with exactly these names and parameters.
In `pizza_price`, choose the base price from the size, then add the toppings.
In `money`, build the string with an f-string.
hints: `def pizza_price(size, toppings=0):` gives toppings a default.
A dictionary like `{"s": 7, ...}` is a neat way to look up the base price.
`clamp` can be done with if/elif/else, or with `min` and `max` together.

static.fail: Don't read input in this test.

cases.fail: Calling your functions printed something. They should only return values.
Running your file on its own should print nothing.
